Back in my day it was all done at your church.  Your minister married you in front of family and friends in the church sanctuary.  The reception was held in the church hall.  If you had a person in the church community that made and decorated cakes you hired and paid her.  The flowers were picked out at a florist shop according to your budget, the dress and veil bought early and paid in full before the wedding.  The tuxedos were picked out and rented.  The rehearsal dinner provided by the parents as was the reception dinner.  
All in all we did not go into debt to marry.  Our family, friends and church community helped out and gladly provided support.  I can tell you this, it was a beautiful wedding and everyone loved it.  This was the norm back then.

comments.author: @ExploreEmbraceExpress
comments.text:
I'll be celebrating my 10 year wedding anniversary right after the new year. My husband and I eloped in Costa Rica.
Because it was just the two of us we saved tens of thousands of dollars. 

My wedding dress was $400, I did my own hair, makeup, and nails. We didn't send out invitations, we didn't have to spend crazy money on food and drinks, all we paid for was the all-inclusive resort which was pretty much empty in January, the photographer which was pretty inexpensive because it was just the two of us, airfare, and of course to actually get our Marriage license.

Altogether we spent about $6000. 
The best part is immediately after our ceremony we were able to have a glass of wine together and then do our photos. 

Once our photos were done we had a private dinner. 

And as soon as dinner ended our honeymoon started. 

I could not emphasize enough how much I encourage people to save money on your wedding day so you can actually enjoy the marriage that comes after it.

The money we saved not going crazy on a wedding, we were able to put $17,000 down on a house that we've been living in for almost 7 years and that now we have close to $80,000 in equity from. 

Remember one of the main reasons people get divorced is financial issues so why would you wanna start your marriage off being broke because you spent so much on a wedding? 

My friend who I've known for over 20 years, she's been married to her husband for 25 years, they had a very simple wedding at a rental hall and their marriage has been wonderful ever since that day, probably in part because it like myself they were able to take money they didn't spend on the wedding and get a beautiful house with it.
